The [paper’s Eq. 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.17152v3) adds relative position/time bias before SiLU. The official research implementation makes alignment explicit: item x_i’s output predicts x_{i+1}, while temporal bias at query i, key j uses t_{i+1}−t_j, not t_i−t_j. Historical timestamps remain aligned with historical item IDs; the bias module shifts query timestamps internally and duplicates the final timestamp at the tensor boundary. The [feature adapter](https://github.com/meta-recsys/generative-recommenders/blob/main/generative_recommenders/research/modeling/sequential/features.py) places the target timestamp immediately after the history, including during offline evaluation. Thus that evaluator has target-time context; deployment needs an available query timestamp or an explicitly chosen fallback.

In [official HSTU code](https://github.com/meta-recsys/generative-recommenders/blob/main/generative_recommenders/research/modeling/sequential/hstu.py), buckets are clamp(long(ln(max(|Δt|,1))/0.301),0,128): natural logarithm, 129 learned temporal entries, plus learned relative-position bias. Missing timestamp payload means None and skips the entire combined position/time bias in this attention path. Individual missing timestamps have no special handling; zero is treated numerically. Masking occurs AFTER SiLU: A=(SiLU(QKᵀ+bias)/N)×M, with an inclusive lower-triangular allowed mask. Padding is removed through jagged sequence lengths; dense conversions zero-pad Q/K/V. A dense LEFT-padded adaptation needs explicit valid-token masking; do not use softmax-style −∞ masking before SiLU.

For this host, the supplied diagnostic batch contains only sequence/positive/negative tensors; log2feats(sequence) exposes no timestamp argument. The task permits timestamps but does not establish an aligned timestamp lookup or inference query time. These remain unverified from the supplied interface. Preserve LEFT-padding alignment and read the final nonpadding position; count−1 applies to the reference’s right-padded layout.
